classes.coverage: Empty by owner decision 34: written only by a language model during bill-family runs, which no scheduled run enables, so no row is produced.

classes.label: Bill activity events
classes.summary: One row per change detected between two runs of the bill family. Two instants per row: `occurred_at` is the publisher's, `detected_at` is the run's. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled: bills the bill family has read from GovInfo BILLSTATUS, Congress by Congress from the 108th on; group by the Congress in bill_id to see which Congresses are filled. Each event compares a bill between two runs of the bill family, not the historical sequence of its actions.
classes.data_quality: A `stage_changed` event compares a bill's actions, not its published stage: the prior stage is re-derived from the bill's published actions under the running stage rule, so a rule change is not an event. spicy-docs 0.51.0 moves 154,374 of the 172,991 stages with actions (its replay, reproduced on the live generation of 2026-09-29), none of which emits one. An event's `from` is therefore the stage the running rule reads from the prior actions, which can differ from the stage the prior row published.

classes.label: Amendments
classes.summary: One row per amendment, from the Congress.gov amendment list and detail routes. Keyed on the amendment's own identity, not the bill it amends, because an amendment can amend another amendment; `amended_bill_id` and `amended_amendment_id` are foreign keys. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Window: the 119th Congress, each amendment with its detail record (the output ledger records its qualification). Scheduled runs walk an `updateDate` window from the table's watermark, at most ninety days, and fetch detail for each amendment in it.
classes.data_quality: The publisher's `updateDate desc` order repeats and skips amendments across page boundaries when stamps tie, so one walk can serve the declared count while missing some amendments. The builder repeats whole walks, alternating order and page size, and settles on the first of two things: a clean walk (no amendment repeated, its distinct count the declared count), which stands alone, or the walks since the count last changed pooled to exactly the declared count. A pool larger than the count is never published, but a later clean walk can still settle; a query unsettled after its walks refuses the run, as does a record without an `updateDate`. Sponsor, chamber, submitted date and the amended bill or amendment come from each amendment's detail record; the list route carries none of them. 89 House amendments name the Rules Committee as sponsor and have no member sponsor to record. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

classes.label: Appropriations press releases
classes.summary: One row per item in one appropriations committee press-release feed capture. `bill_id` is an inferred candidate when a pattern matches a published bill identifier in the title or description. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Window. Releases from the House and Senate Appropriations committees' feeds as captured since September 19, 2026, including items that later rotated out of a feed; bill links are inferred from release text. Not all committees, earlier history or release-page bodies. See `press-release-qualification/` and `press-link-repair/` in the fork execution receipts.
classes.data_quality:
The bill linkage is a pattern match over the release's own words, not a publisher statement. An earlier local run falsely matched `s 2027` inside a reference to the President's 2027 budget to Senate bill 2027. The corrected matcher rejects possessive suffixes while preserving quoted bill citations; wider matching quality remains unmeasured. `matched_field` and `matched_text` carry what was matched and where: a false positive is readable from the row rather than only by re-running the matcher. One pattern is compiled per published bill in the Congresses in scope, bounded on both sides and built from the bill's own type, so a bare number matches nothing. Three states are distinct and must not be read as one: a `bill_id` with `match_rule = bill_number_in_title` or `bill_number_in_excerpt` is a match; `match_rule = unmatched` with a NULL `bill_id` means the matcher ran and found no pattern match; an all-NULL `match_rule` means no matching pass ran at all, because no `congress_bills` table was published when the rollup ran, or none was published for that release's Congress, or the release states no readable `pub_date` to scope by. The Senate feed carries no item description, so a Senate release can only ever match on its title. One consequence worth knowing before relying on these four columns: a run that cannot read `congress_bills` republishes the whole live window with NULL match columns, because this table merges row-wise and a fresh row wins whole. The next run that can read it re-derives them for every release still in the feed, so the gap normally lasts one cycle — but a release that rotates off the feed during that cycle keeps the NULL permanently. The other publisher columns are unaffected; only these four degrade.
The Senate feed stamps every item `EST`, summer included (`Wed, 30 Sep 2026 19:22:00 EST`), and `pub_date_instant` takes the label at its word (`-05:00`); if the feed writes Eastern wall-clock time, an item from March to November reads an hour later than it was posted. (interim until spicy-docs > 0.53.0+laws.f8431033f626)

classes.label: House and Senate roll-call votes
classes.summary: One row per roll call: the publisher's own tally, and the bill it refers to. The four tally columns are the publisher's own counts, NULL on a candidate election (a Speaker vote), whose choices `tallies_json` keeps under their own labels. A Senate count element the file leaves empty or omits (`<present/>`, `<absent/>`) is read as 0, which is what the Senate means by it (119-senate-1-15: 50 yea, 50 nay, 0 present, 0 absent). All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating: both chambers' roll calls from each chamber's own session index (the Senate LIS menu and the House Clerk's EVS index pages, both keyless), newest first under a per-run cap. The scheduled scope is the sitting Congress; an earlier Congress is backfilled by dispatching its number under the same cap and, once held, is never re-read. A roll call already published with a tally is not fetched again, except the newest few of a sitting Congress, re-read in case the publisher corrected them. The Clerk and LIS files reach the 101st Congress (the Clerk's archive begins in 1990, the 101st's second session); the bill family's references reach the 108th. The House files of 1990-2002, the 101st-107th Congresses, are a House-only dispatch (`congresses` 101-107, `chambers` house) run until a run fetches nothing; replayed over the retained Clerk archive through this rollup they refuse none and change no published row (see the output ledger's roll-call row). A set of roll calls reached from bills alone is not an index of a session's roll calls. A House roll call that a bill's own action names can be published a cron before the Clerk's index lists it, with the same tally and member positions. `vote_date` keeps the Clerk's own spelling (`9-Sep-2025`, and `3-JAN-1991` on eight files of 1991-2001), which does not sort as a date, so no range over it is quoted here.
classes.data_quality:
Two statements link a roll call to a bill, and `match_rule` names the one that did. `bill_action_recorded_vote`: a `recordedVotes` entry on the bill's own action, read from `bill_vote_references`. `vote_file_legislation`: the vote file's own statement of its measure, the Clerk's `legis_num` or the Senate's document, with the file's own URL as `match_url`; on a Senate amendment vote that document is `S.Amdt.`, not a bill, so such a roll call links to a bill only where the rollup resolved one through the bill's own recorded-vote action (`count(bill_id)` over amendment votes is the measure). The bill's action wins; where two bills' actions record one roll call, the one the file names wins (the Senate passing a House bill after its Senate twin); with no recorded reference the file links alone. A procedural question, a nomination, a treaty or two different bills link nothing. Measured on the 108th and 119th (receipt `votes-backfill-2026-09-26/file-links/`), the files add 881 links and agree with the recorded reference on 1,803 of the 1,809 roll calls both link; the six others are those Senate passages. `conflict_count` is per roll call, not per run: it counts the later references, the file's included, that named a different bill for *this* roll call, and they are kept rather than dropped. Before 2003 only the file's `legis_num` links: it links 6,614 of the 7,327 files of 1990-2002 to 2,842 bills, 26 of which have no `congress_bills` row yet. A held row is relinked from its own columns without a fetch; a House row published before `legis_num` or `clerk_body_element` existed is read again once to gain both, with `vote_desc`. Replayed over the retained files of the 108th-118th, that read fills the element on all 14,503 published House rows (3,742 `committee`) and `vote_desc` on 9,191, and changes no other column and no member row; it also publishes the five votes the House vacated before recording a position, which have zero tallies, `member_vote_count` 0 and no `member_votes` rows. The Clerk's 2003 Speaker election (108-1-2), whose candidate totals contradict its members' choices, still refuses. The contract's `house_vote_legislation` rule (Congress.gov's `house-vote` listing) is no longer produced and no published row carries it: it was retired with the api.data.gov key it needed (2026-09-26). Each run fills a NULL `vote_day` on every held (completely captured) roll call from its own `vote_date` before merging, so a row published before the column existed gains it without a re-fetch. An incomplete capture is not held: it is re-fetched first each run and takes its day from the file. A linkage-only row keeps NULL.
The vendored `tallies_json` sentence says it holds every count the publisher stated; it holds each roll call's overall totals only, under the publisher's names (the Clerk's `yea-total`, `nay-total`, `present-total` and `not-voting-total`; the Senate's `yeas`, `nays`, `present` and `absent`; a candidate's name in a Speaker election). The Clerk's `totals-by-party` are not carried: count `member_votes` by `party` for a party split, which matched the Clerk's party totals on the House roll calls checked 2026-10-03. (interim until spicy-docs > 0.53.0+laws.f8431033f626)

classes.label: Member vote positions
classes.summary: One row per member's position on one roll call. `position` keeps the publisher's own word (the Clerk spells both Aye/No and Yea/Nay) and `position_normalized` carries the fold, so a count and a quotation are both answerable. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled, and accumulating. One row per member per roll call in `roll_call_votes`, so it inherits that table's both-chambers scope, per-run cap and skip-what-is-already-held behavior exactly.
classes.data_quality:
House rows with `state` `XX` are the non-voting delegates and the Resident Commissioner, as the Clerk marks them. The Clerk marks them only on amendment votes and motions in committee, so leave them out when ranking voting Representatives. A member who died before a term began can appear as Not Voting on its opening quorum call, as the Clerk's file lists them. One `bioguide_id` can carry more than one spelling of `member_name`; group by `bioguide_id`. The Clerk's files of 1990-2002 (the 101st-107th Congresses) name no member by bioguide id: their rows key `name:` plus the Clerk's label (`name:Jones (NC)`) with `bioguide_id` NULL, and that key identifies the row within its roll call, not a person, since at least 21 labels of those years name two different members. `member_vote_terms` leaves such a row `unresolved_member`; no name is matched to a member. Senate rows carry the bioguide id resolved from their LIS id through `members` at the votes merge; a Senate row still NULL has a LIS id that `members` does not hold, or holds twice (`unresolved_member`).
The Clerk lists the Speaker only on the roll calls the Speaker votes on; on the others the Speaker has no row at all, not a Not Voting row (Johnson, J000299, has no row on 54 of the 314 House roll calls of 2026, measured 2026-10-03), so an absence rate over roll calls does not apply to the Speaker. `party` is the label the publisher printed on that roll call, and a change of label starts on the roll call that first prints it: the Clerk prints Kiley (K000401) `R` through roll 95 (2026-03-18) and `I` from roll 96 (2026-03-19), while `member_party_affiliations` dates the change 2026-03-09. Use `party` for a split as the chamber recorded it, and `member_party_affiliations` for a party as of a date.

classes.label: Legislators
classes.summary: One row per legislator in one capture of the community crosswalk. Split from `member_terms` because one row cannot hold a chamber switch. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. The fork selection covers both complete community crosswalk files captured September 22, 2026 UTC: current and historical legislators. Every declared field was checked against the retained originals, and all earlier retained identities and native values survive. The source supplies FEC candidate IDs and LIS IDs for a subset of members; absent IDs remain absent. This qualifies the captured community files, not an independently complete official roster. Receipts: fork-execution-2026-09-21/members-qualification/.

classes.label: Legislator terms
classes.summary: One row per term a legislator served, in the crosswalk's own order. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. The fork selection retains every term from the same complete September 22, 2026 UTC captures as `members`. All mapped values, parent joins and per-member term counts agree with the originals; earlier retained term identities survive. Source order defines term_index. The single party value per term does not reproduce the finer party_affiliations histories, which the crosswalk records only for terms with a mid-term party change; a member with no affiliation interval never switched. Receipts: fork-execution-2026-09-21/members-qualification/.

classes.label: Member party affiliation source intervals
classes.summary: One member, input digest, term index and affiliation index. Literal dates and their parsing states remain separate from any dated membership decision.
classes.coverage: Sampled. The complete retained September 25 community crosswalk captures, replayed and published on September 27; every source affiliation occurrence was reconciled. This is the selected community crosswalk, not an official or newly acquired roster. Receipt: spicy-regs-t19-members-20260927/public-readback.json.

classes.label: Committee reports
classes.summary: One row per published part of a captured GovInfo committee report package, keyed `(package_id, part_id)`. `bill_id` is the measure the report accompanies, read from the package's own MODS metadata. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Selected committee report packages from GovInfo, a mixed-Congress selection that grows as packages are added; not complete historical or constituent-granule coverage. committee_report_reads records each package read and its outcome.
classes.data_quality: Only the MODS PRIMARY bill fills bill_id. The thirteen CBO columns come from spicy-docs read_cbo_estimate on the same body already acquired. The cover recital gates publication of a letter: a CBO heading alone is not an estimate. report_states_estimate=false records an absent recital; NULL means the rule has not run. A positive recital with no resolved letter span remains distinct from an extracted letter. recital_bill_id comes from the printed recital and is retained beside the MODS bill_id. bill_id is the part's own PRIMARY bill: a multi-part package's root states none, so each part of CRPT-119hrpt494 carries the H.R. 3495 its constituent record names, where its row read before parts were keyed has NULL; its separate recital_bill_id is a text interpretation. Every part a record states is read, all or none: a package whose parts cannot all be read is refused in committee_report_reads and keeps its prior rows. Parts, by decision 29 (`docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`): a report published in one part is one row whose part_id is its package id and whose part_number is NULL; a report published as parts is one row per part, part_id the part's granule id (CRPT-119hrpt455-pt2) and part_number 1 to N, except that a Part 1 the publisher left unsuffixed (CRPT-119hrpt494) has part_id equal to the package id and part_number 1. A package whose one part is spelled -pt1 (CRPT-119hrpt811; spicy-docs `docs/tables.md` names the others it measured) is (package-pt1, 1), the same shape as Part 1 of two, so a reader counts a package's rows to tell a lone part from Part 1 of several. title, date_issued and last_modified are the package's and repeat on every part row. A row published before part_id existed is kept as its package's one part (part_id the package id, part_number NULL) until the package is read again, which replaces its rows as a set; the committee_report_reads rule version re-reads every report once for this, which is what re-keys the CRPT-119hrpt811 row published 2026-09-24 as (CRPT-119hrpt811-pt1, 1).

classes.label: Committee report heading and text blocks
classes.summary: One row per heading or unheaded text block in one part of a committee report, keyed `(package_id, part_id, seq)`. `heading` preserves the source title; agency identity fields remain unresolved. `pattern` records which header pattern fired, which is this table's provenance column. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Heading/text blocks of the reports in committee_reports. heading retains the source title while agency_label and agency_key remain unresolved NULLs. HTML bodies carry no page boundaries, so none are inferred.
classes.data_quality: part_id names the committee_reports row a block was parsed from, so (package_id, part_id) is its parent, and seq counts from zero within that part. By decision 29 (`docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`) part_id is the package id for a report published in one part and the part's granule id for a report published as parts, CRPT-119hrpt494's unsuffixed Part 1 aside; a package whose one part is spelled -pt1 (CRPT-119hrpt811; spicy-docs `docs/tables.md` names the others it measured) carries that spelling, so the parent's row count tells a lone part from Part 1 of several. A block published before part_id existed carries its package id there until its report is read again, which replaces every block of the package.

classes.label: Hearing transcripts
classes.summary: One row per captured GovInfo hearing transcript. bill_id is always NULL: a hearing can concern several bills, represented in hearing_bill_links. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Selected hearing packages from GovInfo, each with its native event identifiers checked: package and body metadata, not speaker turns or complete hearing history.
classes.data_quality:
Cover bills come from the package's MODS and cost no extra requests. BODY mentions do not become hearing links. event_id is the meeting the Congress.gov hearing record names (its associatedMeeting), carried as the publisher pairs them. NULL means that record names no meeting, or was refused, and committee_report_reads says which: on committee-reports generation 9aa9d10d… (2026-10-03) all 164 NULL rows were completed reads naming none. It does not mean no meeting exists: a meeting can list the transcript's jacket in `committee_meetings.hearing_jackets_json` without the hearing record naming it. That jacket route is the publisher's many-to-many listing, not a declared join: on committee-meetings generation 31e62420… (2026-10-03) 1,021 meetings list two or more distinct jackets and 1,075 (congress, jacket) values sit on two or more meetings. The declared event_id join reads `complete` because every event_id names a meeting row; that does not check the pairing: CHRG-118hhrg63377 names meeting 116369, an Oversight and Investigations hearing the same day, while its MODS and docs.house.gov place it at 116330. body_completeness says what the read text states about itself: a publisher_placeholder body is the publisher's notice that the document is only in the PDF. When the package offers that PDF it is read instead (pdf_extracted, with text_derivation naming the extraction); when it offers none, the notice is published as it stands. NULL on rows not re-read since the column was added.
`date_issued` is GovInfo's dateIssued, which for a hearing (CHRG) package is the day the hearing was held (a compiled volume's first day), not when the transcript was printed or posted: it equals the meeting's date on all 21 event_id pairs on 2026-10-03. (interim until spicy-docs > 0.53.0+laws.f8431033f626)

classes.label: Hearing-to-bill links
classes.summary: One row per package, bill and link source, shaped by spicy-docs.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Bill references that the selected hearing packages' MODS records state on their cover. It does not show bills named only in constituent records, agendas, bill actions or transcript text, and does not measure recall; agenda acquisition remains deferred.
classes.data_quality: mods_cover means held_on. The package measured confirmation on 19 of 20 cover pairs and 18 of 18 pairs where cover and agenda agreed. Agenda links mean noticed, not held_on: agenda-only pairs were confirmed 1 of 18, contradicted 1 and unverifiable 16. Recall is unmeasured. Only 2 of 20 sampled House hearings and 0 of 3 Senate hearings stated COVER bills; a missing row does not establish that a hearing concerned no bills. A successfully re-read cover replaces that hearing's prior links, including an empty result. Unread or refused bodies retain their prior links. held_date is the one date the hearing's MODS states. A compiled volume that states several dates has held_date NULL and every native date, in source order, in held_dates_json; the list does not establish that each bill was considered on each date. Before link rule d06e0bd80ca1 (2026-09-25) such a volume's links carried its first date (CHRG-117shrg56721 states eleven), and rows not re-read since keep held_dates_json NULL.

classes.label: CBO cost-estimate publication index
classes.summary: One row per bill and CBO publication, using build_bill_family's own cbo_cost_estimates output and spicy-docs' feed builder, merged by `merge_cbo_cost_estimates`: where both routes state one bill and publication, the BILLSTATUS row stands. One publication can stand under two bills, and both rows publish. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled: the estimates CBO lists for the bills the bill family has read, from the 108th Congress on, from two routes merged: each bill's BILLSTATUS record (`source` `billstatus_bulk`) and CBO's own per-Congress feed (`cbo_feed`), read once by every run for each Congress it is scoped to. BILLSTATUS states no estimate for the 112th and 113th, so theirs come from the feed alone; elsewhere the feed adds only what no BILLSTATUS record lists, such as the Recovery Act, H.R. 3200 and the ACA. A Congress no scoped run has read the feed of yet holds its BILLSTATUS estimates only. A feed item that names no bill has no row: CBO's weekly estimates of the bills the House takes up under suspension of the rules, a committee's reconciliation recommendations, and an estimate CBO files under no bill number. A bill passed under suspension can be scored in such a weekly estimate first or only, so its first row here does not date CBO's first estimate of it. An absent estimate does not mean CBO never scored a bill. No CBO.gov body is requested.
classes.data_quality: The bill's cbo_cost_estimates_outcome distinguishes an absent or empty element, an unexpected shape, and populated estimates. An empty index does not establish that CBO never scored the bill. Report citations are the bill's list, not proof that each publication is reprinted in each report; the report's recital gate is evaluated separately. A feed row carries its bill's own BILLSTATUS report citations, read by the same run or carried from the bill's published rows, and NULL where neither names them. A successfully evaluated bill replaces its prior BILLSTATUS rows, including when the list is absent or empty; an unexpected list shape retains prior rows until a successful read can establish the current relationships. A feed read replaces its Congress's prior feed rows, so an item CBO withdraws or re-files leaves, and a feed that cannot be read keeps them. `found_by` says how each row names its bill; the rows published before it take `billstatus` in a one-time backfill. `title_bill_id` is the bill the estimate's title leads with: where it differs from `bill_id` (7 of the 12,732 BILLSTATUS rows on 2026-09-29), `bill_id` is a numbering error as published and `title_bill_id` the bill scored. A title leading with a public law reads through the published `laws` table, which held the 119th Congress alone on 2026-09-29, so such a title of an earlier Congress leaves `title_bill_id` NULL and a blank feed item titled by an earlier law has no row (110th P.L. 110-50 and 112th P.L. 112-8). CBO's 119th-Congress feed, read 2026-10-03, holds 53 items that name no bill and have no row, 48 of them weekly suspension estimates. 23 of them are among the feed's 674 items dated 2026: 21 suspension estimates, 62413 (reconciliation recommendations of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs committee) and 62643 (the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027).

classes.label: Enacted laws
classes.summary: One row per enacted law the Congress.gov law list route states, with the Statutes at Large citation from the law's own PLAW USLM file where captured. Keyed on the law's Congress, type and number, not on the bill; `bill_id` is the foreign key to `congress_bills`, whose `statutes_at_large_cite` the host fills from this table at that table's merge. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Every law the Congress.gov law route lists for the scoped Congresses (the current one by default), walked whole each run; the PLAW USLM citation is added per law, newest first, under a per-run cap. A steady-state run is meant to ask only about laws whose list row moved or whose PLAW the bulk folder had not yet served.
classes.data_quality:
`statutes_at_large_cite` is set when `uslm_outcome` is `captured`; read every NULL through `uslm_outcome` and `uslm_reason`. `unavailable` (reason `source_unavailable`) is the publisher's own lag, a `404` from the exact PLAW locator: on 2026-09-19 the route listed 108 laws and the PLAW bulk folder held 104, the four newest (119-103, 119-104, 119-109, 119-110) absent; each is retried every run until the folder serves it.
`captured_partial` is a validated USLM file that states no Statutes at Large citation (reason `statutes_citation_not_stated`): the two private laws of the 119th (`PLAW-119pvtl1`, `PLAW-119pvtl2`), whose own `citableAs` values are kept in `uslm_citable_as_json`. Until reader rule `laws-uslm-v2` (2026-09-25) the contract refused those two files and their rows said `not_requested`, although both were requested and served. `captured_refused` keeps the digest of a `200` body the reader refused, either another law's file (`native_identity_refused`) or not native USLM at all, such as an HTML page (`native_shape_refused`), and none of its unvalidated fields. `request_failed` is an attempted read that established nothing, a transport failure included; it is never published as `unavailable`. `not_requested` means only that no request was made, which the per-run cap decides.
A validated row with parsed text is read again when its listing or metadata/text reader changes, or its matching section output is missing. A failed later attempt preserves its prior metadata and parsed sections. `law_text_outcome` distinguishes unread, parsed and refused text; an unavailable XML file does not mean the law has no provisions. Join `law_sections` on `law_id` for native sections. `law_body_remainder` retains main-body text outside those sections, including appropriation blocks; it is NULL unless parsed and may be an empty string on success. The section rows and remainder are printed law text, not consolidated current law. A publisher-refused Table III read is journaled `table3-bulk-refused` with reason `access-refused`, and the laws family publishes without the Table III rows that read would have added. `statutes_at_large_volume` follows the session that cleared the bill, not the year the law was approved: 119-69 and 119-71 to 119-73, approved in January 2026 on bills cleared in December 2025, are in volume 139, and 119-70 and 119-74 on are in volume 140. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
Two vendored column sentences are wrong. `latest_action_date` is not the became-law action but the publisher's latest action, which can follow enactment (119-public-68: a committee report filed 2026-02-11 after approval on 2025-12-29). For the enactment date use `approved_date`, else `congress_bills.signed_date` through `bill_id` (NULL on a private law, rule `no_public_law`). `uslm_observed_at` is not only a capture time: it is when the read this row's outcome states got its response, the 404 on an `unavailable` row included, and NULL when no read was attempted or the attempt got no response. (interim until spicy-docs > 0.53.0+laws.f8431033f626)

classes.label: Published law sections

Section numbers and publisher IDs can repeat or be absent; (law_id, seq) identifies each occurrence and native_path locates it in the source XML. is_quoted marks sections inside quotedContent; parent_seq alone does not imply a quotation. Body excludes its own number and heading, print furniture, and nested sections' text; query the child rows as well. laws.law_body_remainder retains text outside all numbered sections, including appropriation blocks. Hierarchy and issues_json retain context and source irregularities. All columns are VARCHAR, including boolean and numeric observations.
classes.coverage: Derived: source-native sections from identity-validated GovInfo public and private law XML acquired by the laws rollup. Join law_id to laws.law_id, then laws.bill_id to congress_bills.bill_id. A missing section row does not establish that the law has no text: check laws.law_text_outcome and law_section_count. Coverage follows successfully read XML, not all enacted laws. PDF-only sources are outside this reader.
classes.data_quality: Under `reader_version` `law-sections-uslm-v1`, every row of laws generation c1ed486d… (2026-10-03), the USLM margin notes are lines of `body`, unflagged: citation notes such as `42 USC 405 note.`, the approval date, catchwords such as `Contracts.`; `issues_json` names only page furniture, though the vendored `body` sentence says print furniture is excluded. Remove them before quoting; the same holds for `laws.law_body_remainder`. Reader `law-sections-uslm-v2` excludes them as print furniture. (interim until spicy-docs > 0.53.0+laws.f8431033f626)

classes.label: Law classifications by Congress
classes.summary: One row per line of an OLRC per-Congress classification table: a U.S. Code place one public law section touched, with the Statutes at Large page and the publisher's action word. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Every row of each public-law-order table the OLRC classification index links for a scoped Congress, read whole every run and replacing that session's rows. The index links the current Congress's session tables only.
classes.data_quality: A row is its position on the page (`seq`), because one line can repeat; a page read this run replaces every prior row for its Congress and session, so a line the publisher removed does not linger under a position it no longer holds. A session not read keeps its rows, and `observed_at` says when they were read. On 2026-10-02 and -03 OLRC answered its classification pages with a maintenance page and status 200, which the reader refuses rather than reading as an empty table. A refused page, or a 401/403, is journaled as `classification-refused` with its URL, status and time, and the nightly `scripts/check_source_refusals.py` fails while the current laws generation holds one; a 401/403 that leaves no session table read also fails the laws run after it publishes. A transport failure is only retried on the next run. Only the public-law order is read: the code-order twin holds the same lines under positions that would collide with these. A Congress the index does not link — every Congress but the current one — gets no rows here; `table3_records` is the historical view. `action` is the page's column 3 verbatim, NULL where the page left it blank, which its legend reads as amended. `usc_section_key` is `usc_section` folded for joins (trimmed, lower-cased, every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen), because case carries no identity in the Code and a join on the printed letter misses the upper-case spellings (decision 30, `docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`); a session's next read replaces its rows, which fills the key for rows published before the column existed. A law can be classified in the session table after the one its number suggests (119-70 is in the session-2 table, whose caption names it); filter by `law_id`, not by `session`, and `stated_laws` carries each table's caption. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

classes.label: Table III records
classes.summary: One row per classification record of one public law in OLRC's Table III: which U.S. Code place each section of the law went to, as Table III's bulk file states it. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Window, complete for the Congresses read: every public law Table III holds for each Congress the laws table holds, plus the scoped ones, derived from OLRC's Table III bulk file on each run, so a Congress keeps its rows current after it leaves the laws scope while Table III catches up. The file holds the whole table back to 1789; other Congresses, private laws and pre-1957 session-law chapters are not derived.
classes.data_quality:
Table III holds an act only once OLRC has classified it, and lags enactment: on 2026-09-26 it was current through 119-73, a law of 2026-01-23, while the law route reached 119-111. `release_point` says how current the file was.
Since 2026-09-26 the rows come from the bulk file (`fulldump@<release point>.xml`) instead of one page per act. The file splits an act's records about ten to an `<act>` fragment. An act's rows are its fragments' records in the file's order, and `seq` is a record's position in its act, as on the page; the file's own `sequence` attribute repeats within 70 acts, so it is not used. Each fragment states its own Congress, date and Statutes volume, and a record carries its fragment's volume where it states a page. Replayed against the 2,981 rows the pages had published, every row keeps its position, act section, Statutes page and volume, Code title and section, status and release point. The file also holds 119-30 and 119-53, whose pages the page walk never reached. Four act-level columns now carry the file's spelling instead of the page's: `stated_key` `119-37` (page `119–37`), `congress` `119` (`119th Cong.`), `act_date` `2025-11-12` (`Nov. 12, 2025`) and `statutes_at_large_volume` `139` (`139 Stat.`).
OLRC states no Last-Modified, ETag or Content-Length for the zip, so each run fetches it; it was byte-identical on 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-26 at the same release point. Each Congress keeps a checkpoint in the file's metadata: the derivation rule with a digest of SpicyDocs' code (not its release string, so a version-only release derives nothing), the member's digest and release point, and each act's shaped-row digest. While all match, nothing is derived. Otherwise every scoped act is derived again, and only an act whose rows changed is published, its whole row set replaced.
Table III only grows: across the eight consecutive releases from 116-150 (2020-07) to 119-73, archived by the Wayback Machine, no act was ever dropped (receipt `table3-bulk-2026-09-26/wayback/`). So a held act the file no longer lists loses its rows only when the release point advances, at most one act a release, and the removal is journaled as `rows-retired` for qualification to reconcile. A file whose release point is older than the one published, that drops an act without advancing, or that drops more than one is refused, and so is a file the reader refuses outright: the member has been renamed twice since 2020. A refused read publishes nothing for this table and keeps every checkpoint, while `laws` and `law_code_sections` publish as usual. The build journals it as `table3-bulk-refused`, and the nightly `scripts/check_source_refusals.py` fails while the current laws generation holds one, so the table cannot stop updating in silence. A transport failure is only retried on the next run. `usc_section_key` is `usc_section` folded for joins (trimmed, lower-cased, every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen), because case carries no identity in the Code and Table III itself prints some sections both ways (decision 30, `docs/research/fork-delivery-decisions-2026-09-22.md`). All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

classes.label: Committees
classes.summary: One row per committee or subcommittee of any Congress the Congress.gov committee list route states, keyed on the publisher's `systemCode`, with the detail record's history, subcommittees, parent and currency folded on where captured. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Since 2026-09-26 the Congress.gov committee route is walked whole with no Congress: every committee of every Congress the publisher records, because `committee_meetings` keeps the previous Congress and `bill_committees` reaches the 108th. The committee detail is folded onto each row under a per-run cap, newest `update_date` first; a committee whose detail was captured is re-read only when its list row's `update_date` moves. Receipt `committee-fixes-2026-09-26/3-rosters-118/`.
classes.data_quality: The route over-declares: on 2026-09-19 `committee/119` declared 238 and served 236 on its one terminal page with no continuation. The reader's terminal-page count refusal is the one refusal this rollup reads past, publishing what the publisher served with both numbers in the run log; every other walk refusal fails the run. `detail_captured` says whether the detail's columns are the publisher's or NULL; where the detail was captured, its `subcommittees` are the row's, an empty list included. The detail's counts (`bill_count` and the rest) are that day's statement, dated by `detail_update_date`. Rows are committees of every Congress: filter `is_current` for today's. 95 historical committees are keyed on their Library of Congress name-authority id (`n79043125`, the Senate's Indian Affairs, 1820-1946), which their history states as `locLinkedDataId`; none is current. A code the detail route cannot address is a list row with `detail_captured` false. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

classes.label: Committee assignments
classes.summary: One row per member per committee or subcommittee seat a chamber roster file lists today, from the House Clerk's MemberData.xml and the Senate's cvc_member_data.xml. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.
classes.coverage: Sampled. Today's seats: the House Clerk's and the Senate's committee files are captured whole each run, for the current Congress only, and each capture replaces its chamber's rows for that Congress; an earlier Congress keeps its last capture. Vacant and placeholder seats appear as the Clerk's file states them.
classes.data_quality: A row is a seat the file listed on its `file_date`: a seat the file no longer lists is gone on the next capture. The House file states its Congress and the reader proves it; the Senate file states none, so its rows carry the caller's Congress with `congress_basis` = `caller`. A House vacancy has no member and no row, and a seated member whose only assignment is the file's `<committee rank=""/>` placeholder has none either (nine placeholders on 2026-09-19). Only a file captured this run replaces its chamber's rows; a chamber whose file was not established keeps its prior rows. House `system_code` derives its prefix from the native committee type and parent context; `committee_code` preserves the literal source identifier. Join matching `system_code` values to `committees` and `bioguide_id` to `members`. Rows whose `system_code` matches no committee stay listed and are never matched by name (the Joint Economic Committee has three Congress.gov codes). On 2026-09-23 that is 28 rows: 25 House seats on the Clerk's four joint committees (`EC00`, `IT00`, `JL00`, `JP00`, typed `joint` in the Clerk file with no Congress.gov code), and three Senate seats on `JSIK00`, the 2024 inaugural committee, which Congress.gov does not list in any Congress. All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

classes.label: Federal Register documents
classes.summary: One row per dated Federal Register record, keyed by (`document_number`, `publication_date`), ingested from the federalregister.gov REST API by `build_federal_register`. The authoritative rule-publication record — proposed rules, final rules, and notices — complementary to the regulations.gov `dockets`/`documents` view. `regulation_id_numbers_json` (RIN) and `cfr_references_json` are the join keys to the Unified Agenda and the CFR. All columns are stored as VARCHAR; array-valued fields are JSON.
classes.coverage: True range: dated records published from 1994-01-03 on, the whole span the API serves.
classes.data_quality: Document numbers are not globally unique: `00-111` names different records on 2000-01-14 and 2000-01-18. Current merging preserves both dates and replaces only the same dated record on a later successful fetch. This code correction does not restore historical records already lost from published files; those require a pinned historical replay and publication. A number-only source reference remains ambiguous when its input generation supplies multiple dated candidates. One RIN, docket and title can cover a rule and its later corrections, effective-date delays and confirmations, all typed `Rule` since 2008 with `subtype` NULL, so a RIN or title match picks a document family, not a document; tell them apart by title, abstract and `publication_date`. The API lists no RIN on a large share of `Rule` documents every year, some of which state one in the printed text or inside `docket_ids_json`.

Codes stay literal. `fec_committees` is the current registry from the API; this is the history, keyed on (`committee_id`, `cycle`). All columns are stored as VARCHAR.

classes.coverage: True range. Every cycle from 1980 through the current one: each run reads every cycle's bulk candidate master whole and publishes every row. The current cycle's file is republished daily, so its rows change.

classes.coverage: True range. Every docket record in the Mirrulations mirror, read whole by `run-attributes-sweep` and kept current by the daily regulations ETL. DocSpec's API capture of 2026-09-02 is the input baseline (receipt `regulations-attributes-20260926/`); the published count is the live pin.

classes.label: Regulations.gov comment attributes
classes.summary: One row per Regulations.gov comment, keyed by `comment_id`, with the attributes the thin `comments` table does not carry: the submitter's stated address, city, state, postal code, country and representative (decision 66), the submitting government body and its level, tracking number, object handle, page count, postmark date, withdrawal flag and reason, access restriction, legacy id, the comment's own content-file renditions and the agency's display properties.
